labels_from.note: Labels are the paper's \label names; `map_steps` are its neutral proof-step labels. scripts/build-site.py --statement-map checks the Lean names against that file.

conventions: Rings are associative and unital; modules are right modules; products are read in the written order. An element is regular if it is a left and right non-zero-divisor. Kdim is the right deviation (Gabriel-Rentschler) dimension. A module is Goldie-torsion if every element is killed by a regular element.
hypotheses: the centre of R is infinite
Kdim(R/dR) is finite for every regular d

results.label: thm:Aprime
results.title: Theorem A′
results.name: fixed ideal
results.short: (S)(N)(Z); I ∋ regular, Kdim(R/I) < ∞ ⇒ ∀x, ∀t ≠ 0 ∃H: I + (x + Ht)R = R
results.statement: Assume (S), (N), (Z). Let I be a right ideal that contains a regular element and has Kdim(R/I) finite. For every x and every nonzero t in R there is H with I + (x + Ht)R = R.

steps.text: Theorem A′ is the last stage P(N+1) of the two-call descent, run with no tests: Kdim R/(I + fR) < 0, that is, I + fR = R.

results.label: thm:A
results.title: Theorem A
results.name: fixed anchor
results.short: (S)(N)(Z); d regular, Kdim(R/dR) < ∞ ⇒ ∀a ≠ 0, ∀B ∃H, U, V: 1 = dU + (B + Ha)dV
results.statement: Assume (S), (N), (Z). Let d be regular with Kdim(R/dR) finite. For every nonzero a (possibly a zero-divisor) and every B there are H, U, V with 1 = dU + (B + Ha)dV. For a = 1, B = 0 this is Stafford's identity R = dR + HdR.

steps.text: Apply Theorem A′ to I = dR, x = Bd and t = ad, which is nonzero because d is regular.
Then I + (x + Ht)R = dR + (B + Ha)dR = R, which is 1 = dU + (B + Ha)dV.

results.label: cor:B
results.title: Corollary B
results.name: Kdim R ≤ ω
results.short: (N), Kdim R ≤ ω ⇒ Kdim(R/I) < ∞ for every I ∋ regular; so A and A′ hold for all such d, I
results.statement: If R is right Noetherian with Kdim R ≤ ω, then Kdim(R/I) is finite for every right ideal I containing a regular element. Hence, under (S), (N), (Z), Theorem A holds for every regular d and Theorem A′ for every such I. (The ordinal refinement δ(d) < Kdim R is not formalized.)

steps.text: For regular d the chain R ⊇ dR ⊇ d²R ⊇ ⋯ has every factor isomorphic to R/dR, so Kdim R ≤ ω forces Kdim(R/dR) finite (lemma Hall).
A right ideal containing a regular s contains sR, so R/I is a quotient of R/sR.
Theorems A and A′ then apply with this finite bound.

results.label: prop:C1
results.title: Corollary C.1
results.name: cyclicity
results.short: M finite Goldie-torsion, Kdim M < ∞ ⇒ ∀x ∈ M, ∀t ≠ 0 ∃h: M = (x + ht)R
results.statement: Assume (S), (N), (Z). If M is a finite Goldie-torsion module with Kdim M finite, then for every x in M and nonzero t in R there is h in M with M = (x + ht)R. Under (H_all), in particular under (H_ω), the dimension hypothesis holds for every finite Goldie-torsion M. Stable form: if c, u are Goldie-torsion and Kdim(uR) is finite, then cR + uR = (c + uHt)R for some H.

steps.text: Stable form: choose a regular b with cb = 0; Theorem A′ for the annihilator of u, with offset 0 and tail tb, gives 1 = i + Htbr with ui = 0. For z = c + uHt this gives z(br) = u, so u and c lie in zR.
Prescribed generator: induction on a finite generating set; each new generator is absorbed into the current affine generator x + yt by the stable form.
Under (H_all) each cyclic submodule uR ≅ R/ann(u) is a quotient of R/sR for a regular s, so its dimension is finite.

results.label: prop:C2
results.title: Corollary C.2
results.name: two generators
results.short: (H_all) ⇒ every right ideal I = aR + (y + ht)R, for any a with aQ = IQ, y ∈ I, t ≠ 0
results.statement: Assume (S), (N), (Z), (H_all). Every right ideal I is generated by two elements. More precisely, if a in I satisfies aQ = IQ (Q the classical right quotient ring), then for every y in I and nonzero t there is h in I with I = aR + (y + ht)R.

steps.text: An element a ∈ I with aQ = IQ exists by Goldie's theorem.
For such a, I/aR is finite and Goldie-torsion, and C.1 applied to y + aR gives h ∈ I with I = aR + (y + ht)R.

results.label: prop:C3
results.title: Corollary C.3
results.name: generator bounds
results.short: (H_all) ⇒ ⌈ρ(M)⌉ ≤ μ(M) ≤ ⌊ρ(M)⌋ + 1 for finite M (ρ normalized Goldie rank)
results.statement: Assume (S), (N), (Z), (H_all). For every finite module M, ⌈ρ(M)⌉ ≤ μ(M) ≤ ⌊ρ(M)⌋ + 1, where μ is the minimal number of generators and ρ(M) = length_Q(M ⊗_R Q)/s for Q = M_s(D). The lower bound needs only (S), (N). The Lean statement encodes ρ through uniform dimensions: s = udim(R_R) and length_Q(M ⊗_R Q) = udim(M/t(M)).

steps.text: Lower bound: if m elements generate M, then M ⊗ Q is a quotient of Q^m, so l ≤ ms.
Upper bound, base case l < s: choose fractions spanning M ⊗ Q one simple summand at a time; the rest is Goldie-torsion and C.1 with an unused idempotent index gives one generator.
Upper bound, step l ≥ s: an element p with pR ≅ R_R exists, M/pR has rank l − s, and induction on q gives q generators when l < qs. No matrix-ring transfer is used.

results.label: thm:apps-a
results.title: Applications (a)
results.name: filtered rings
results.short: simple k-algebra, k infinite, gr commutative Noetherian of finite Krull dimension: A, A′, B, C on both sides
results.statement: Let k be an infinite field and R a simple k-algebra with an exhaustive filtration whose associated graded ring is commutative Noetherian of Krull dimension at most m. Then R and its opposite ring satisfy (N), (Z) and Kdim ≤ m, and Theorem A, Theorem A′, Corollary B and Corollaries C.1-C.3 hold on both sides.

results.label: thm:apps-b
results.title: Applications (b)
results.name: Weyl algebras
results.short: A_n(k), char k = 0: 1 = dR + HdR (Stafford's Conjecture 3.8); A, A′, C.1, C.2 on both sides
results.statement: For the Weyl algebra A_n(k) over a field of characteristic zero: for every nonzero d there are F, R, S with 1 = dR + FdS (Stafford's Conjecture 3.8); Theorem A and Theorem A′ in affine form; finitely generated torsion modules are cyclic with a prescribed generator; right and left ideals are two-generated, with a prescribed first generator.

results.label: thm:apps-c
results.title: Applications (c)
results.name: differential operators
results.short: D_k(A), A smooth affine domain, char k = 0: 1 = dR + FdS; A, C.1, C.2 on both sides
results.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic zero and A a smooth domain of finite type over k, with D_k(A) its ring of differential operators. Right and left ideals of D_k(A) are two-generated; Theorem A holds in right and left form; for every nonzero d there are F, R, S with 1 = dR + FdS; finitely generated torsion right and left modules are cyclic with a prescribed generator.

results.label: thm:apps-d
results.title: Applications (d)
results.name: enveloping algebras
results.short: simple quotients of U(𝔤), 𝔤 finite-dimensional, k infinite: (N), (Z), Kdim ≤ dim 𝔤; A, A′, B, C on both sides
results.statement: For a finite-dimensional Lie algebra 𝔤 over an infinite field k and a simple quotient R of U(𝔤): R and its opposite ring are Noetherian, have infinite centre and Kdim ≤ dim 𝔤, and Theorem A, Theorem A′, Corollary B and Corollaries C.1-C.3 hold on both sides.

results.label: thm:apps-e
results.title: Applications (e)
results.name: simple quantizations
results.short: simple filtered k-algebra, gr a commutative Noetherian domain of finite Krull dimension: Theorem A for all nonzero d, both sides
results.statement: If R is a simple algebra over an infinite field k with an exhaustive filtration whose associated graded ring is a commutative Noetherian domain of finite Krull dimension (for instance gr R ≅ ℂ[X] for an irreducible affine variety X), then for every nonzero d and a and every B there are H, U, V with 1 = dU + (B + Ha)dV, and 1 = Ud + Vd(B + aH).

lemmas.label: lem:unit
lemmas.title: Unit germs
lemmas.short: q_K r is epic ⇔ Kdim R/(K + rR) < e

lemmas.label: lem:epic
lemmas.title: Epic criterion
lemmas.short: a germ is epic ⇔ P_w is injective on every simple top factor

lemmas.label: lem:strata
lemmas.title: Finite top strata
lemmas.short: Kdim X ≤ e ⇒ the top stratum of X has finite length; it vanishes ⇔ Kdim X < e
lemmas.missing: Not stated in Lean: the formal proof has no quotient functor F_e; it works with germs and critical filtrations instead.

lemmas.label: lem:pencil
lemmas.title: Pencils
lemmas.short: P + φ_λP′ injective for all but finitely many central λ; so an epic germ v stays epic along v + uλ

lemmas.label: lem:escape
lemmas.title: Escape
lemmas.short: g ≠ 0, t′ ≠ 0 ⇒ gRt′ lies in no finite-dimensional E-subspace

lemmas.label: lem:rank
lemmas.title: Maximal rank
lemmas.short: P injective, t′ ≠ 0 ⇒ some H makes h ↦ P(h)Ht′ injective

lemmas.label: lem:select
lemmas.title: Source selection
lemmas.short: some f = x + Ht satisfies any finite list of germ tests; tests survive f + λg for almost all λ

steps.text: Step 1: by induction on the pairs (test, simple top factor), maximal rank and ordinary pencils give H₀ making every map h ↦ P_i(h)H₀tc_i injective.
Step 2: the offset maps form reversed pencils in a central λ; a good λ gives H = λH₀.
Pencil stability: z + q(f + λg)c = (z + qfc) + (qgc)λ because λ is central.

lemmas.title: Two-call descent
lemmas.short: P(h) ⇒ P(h+1): two calls of P(h) and a central scalar lower Kdim R/(I + fR) by one

steps.text: Base P(0): source selection gives f = x + Ht satisfying the tests; R/(I + fR) is a quotient of R/I.
1. First call: f = x + Ht satisfies the tests and J = I + fR has Kdim R/J ≤ e.
2. Torsion equation: a regular b with fb ∈ I (Goldie's theorem).
3. Second call, same I: offset 0, tail tb and the single unit test of R/J give gb with Q = I + gbR.
4. Vanishing of the joint top: J + gbR = Q + fR, so v = q_Q f is epic.
5. Good central scalar: a nonzero λ ∈ k outside the finitely many exceptions.
6. Pencil inclusion: gbλ = (f + λg)b − fb, so Q ⊆ J′ = I + (f + λg)R.
7. Drop: q_Q(f + λg) = v + uλ is epic, so Kdim R/J′ < e.
8. Affine form: f + λg = x + (H + λH₂)t.
Termination: N + 1 steps reach Kdim R/(I + fR) < 0, with N = Kdim(R/I).

lemmas.label: lem:Hall
lemmas.title: Lemma Kdim ≤ ω
lemmas.short: Kdim R ≤ ω ⇒ Kdim(R/dR) < ∞ for regular d, and Kdim(R/I) < ∞ for I ∋ regular

lemmas.title: C.3 rank induction
lemmas.short: Goldie rank l < qs ⇒ q generators; base case l < s gives a cyclic module
